findings.text: BPF helper exposes cache lookup from an address. Invalid virtual addresses yield null. Valid addresses that map to a slab yield the owning cache, otherwise null.

Nolock RCU free attempts a sheaf fast path for slab objects on the local NUMA node when batched RCU freeing is enabled. Vmalloc addresses, missing slab association, remote NUMA placement, or sheaf rejection all divert to deferred handling through the supplied head.

Simplified RCU free either schedules asynchronous reclaim when a head is present or performs synchronous grace wait followed by immediate release when no head is given. Barrier in this variant combines deferred work drain with RCU barrier, and initialization does nothing.

Batched RCU free accepts slab and vmalloc pointers with or without an embedded head. Headless use requires sleepable context. Objects first try per CPU sheaf insertion outside realtime configurations, then bulk queueing, then linked head queueing when bulk resources are exhausted, with synchronous fallback when queueing without a head fails.

Sheaf insertion batches a single object into the current CPU active RCU sheaf. Empty active state triggers reuse of spare resources or acquisition of empty containers from node storage or fresh allocation. Reaching capacity detaches the full container for grace based reclamation while a non full container stays active.
Deferral path enqueues a head onto per CPU deferred RCU object state under a non preemptible region and requests interrupt driven draining when the queue transitions from empty.

Global sheaf flush drains deferred work, then iterates known slab caches under machine wide CPU and cache list protection to flush each cache that supports sheaves, then waits for RCU completion. Full barrier combines this flush with the generic RCU free barrier.
Bulk container groups linkage in list plus grace information in gp_snap plus occupancy in nr_records plus payload in records where records length follows nr_records.
Per batch work record bundles control in rcu_work plus head list in head_free plus snapshot in head_free_gp_snap plus per channel bulk lists in bulk_head_free plus owner in krcp.

Per CPU reclaim state front portion holds direct queue in head with snapshot in head_gp_snap and tally in head_count plus bulk queues in bulk_head with tallies in bulk_count plus batch array in krw_arr plus protection in lock plus monitor scheduling in monitor_work plus readiness in initialized.

Per CPU reclaim state rear portion holds refill scheduling in page_cache_work plus refill control in backoff_page_cache_fill and work_in_progress plus timing in hrtimer plus empty block caching in bkvcache with occupancy in nr_bkv_objs. Storage is per CPU named krc with static lock setup.
Normal monitor delay spans five HZ intervals. Batch work array holds two entries. Bulk handling uses two channels distinguishing slab origin from vmalloc origin.
Maximum records per bulk block equals page size minus header size divided by pointer size, defining when a new block must be obtained.

Reclaim tuning defaults keep five cached empty bulk blocks per CPU and delay refill backoff by five thousand milliseconds. Reclaim monitor work runs on a dedicated workqueue pointer held in rcu_reclaim_wq.

Usable size equals object_size when debugging combines with SLAB_RED_ZONE or SLAB_POISON and also when SLAB_KASAN is set. Usable size equals inuse when SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU or SLAB_STORE_USER is set and also when object extensions reside inside the object. Otherwise usable size equals size.

Queueing classifies pointers by vmalloc residence into channel one versus channel zero and stamps the active bulk block with a full grace snapshot on every insertion while incrementing the matching channel tally.

Reclamation proceeds only after grace observation succeeds for the associated snapshot. Bulk blocks are examined from oldest toward newest with early stop on first unready block, and direct head lists require their snapshot to be ready before release.

Total backlog sums direct and bulk tallies across channels. Monitor rescheduling uses a minimal delay when backlog reaches bulk capacity and otherwise uses the normal drain interval, shortening an already pending timer only when the new delay is earlier.

Per CPU reclaim state is guarded by its raw spin lock in lock with interrupt save and restore around acquisition. Local CPU acquisition disables interrupts before resolving the per CPU pointer to keep pointer lookup stable, and release restores the saved interrupt state.

Sheaf insertion uses nonblocking try acquisition of the per cache CPU sheaf lock and abandons fast path on contention, with ordering map held outside realtime builds and no spinning under realtime. Global sheaf flush holds CPU read protection and slab_mutex while walking the cache list and skipping entries lacking sheaf support.

Empty bulk blocks are cached per CPU up to a small bound, activated as channel heads, filled until capacity, then detached for grace gated reclaim. After reclaim each block is either returned to the per CPU empty cache or released as a page, with background refill and explicit drain paths maintaining the cache.

Sheaf objects accumulate until capacity then transfer to RCU callback handling, with interrupt deferred queueing when non spinning context is interrupted with interrupts disabled. Monitor work repeatedly drains ready objects, queues remaining batches, and rearms itself while offload remains needed. Page cache refill uses timer driven high priority work or delayed reclaim work under backoff.

Headless freeing from non sleepable context is unsafe and debug double queueing leaks instead of corrupting. Sheaf use is disabled under realtime for certain callers to avoid wait lock acquisition, and remote NUMA or vmalloc inputs bypass sheaf handling. Flushing before local unlock prevents races with concurrent global flush, and reclaim work avoids waking reclaim paths that could deadlock under scheduler locks.

Shrinker accounting sums queued objects and cached empty blocks across all CPUs and simultaneously arms refill backoff to shed cache pressure, reporting empty when nothing is held. Scheduler startup walks all CPUs and arms monitor work wherever offload remains pending.

Work callbacks provide monitor draining, bulk and head reclaim, empty block refill, and timer based refill dispatch. Reclaim distinguishes slab bulk release via bulk free from vmalloc bulk release via individual release and handles direct head chains via generic virtual free.

Debug object tracking unqueues bulk and direct entries at reclaim time and queueing time, with queue time failure treated as double free and leaked with a one time warning. Trace and lockdep style acquire release annotations bracket callback invocation.
